headline: Frozen protein-model embeddings rank enzymes, substrates and mutants under harder tests
label: Learned Enzyme And Variant Prioritization
summary: Kinetics, EC assignment, stability and binding-site predictors now sit on frozen PLM/structure encoders, paired with campaign-grouped benchmarks and wet-lab checks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is ranking enzyme-related candidates with representations lifted from pretrained protein and chemical models: KineCouple applies substrate-conditioned cross-attention over frozen ProtT5/MolT5 features for kcat and Km, DecoyOpt uses ESM3-generated functional-site decoys to separate active enzymes and assign EC numbers, StableProt couples SaProt with Foldseek 3Di tokens for Tm and OGT, and a fungal peroxygenase workflow chains sequence mining, expression-aware prioritization, gradient boosting and screening. What is new is the evaluation turn. EnzyArena groups kinetic data by engineering campaign, compares 20 models, finds zero-shot consensus strongest and validates on 150 mutants; systematic reviews and ligand-aware benchmarks probe EC and binding-site generalization; OneProt profiling attributes performance largely to dataset separability. Diagnostics temper the embeddings: PLM contact maps collapse under amino-acid relabeling, and NMR chemical shifts expose errors at dynamic core residues.
